Differential item functioning (DIF) in one call

Source: R/dif.R
dif.Rd

Tests every item for DIF between groups (for example by gender or language) and reports the results as a tidy table with effect sizes. The analysis uses the constrained-baseline approach: a multiple-group model is fitted with all item parameters equal across groups and free latent means and variances, then each item's parameters are freed in turn and compared with a likelihood-ratio test (mirt::DIF() with scheme = "drop").

Usage

dif(
  x,
  group = NULL,
  model = "2PL",
  items = NULL,
  which.par = NULL,
  p_adjust = "BH",
  alpha = 0.05,
  verbose = FALSE,
  ...
)

Arguments

x

a data frame or matrix of item responses, or a mirt::multipleGroup() model whose item parameters are constrained to be equal across groups (the baseline model).

group

the grouping variable: a vector with one value per respondent, or the name of a column of x (that column is then not treated as an item). Ignored when x is a model.

model

item type passed to mirt::multipleGroup(), e.g. "Rasch", "2PL", "3PL", "graded" or "gpcm". Ignored when x is a model.

items

items to test, by name or position. Defaults to all items; untested items act as anchors.

which.par

parameters to test. Defaults to all estimated item parameters (for example a1 and d for the 2PL).

p_adjust

p-value adjustment across items (see stats::p.adjust()).

alpha

significance level for flagging an item, applied to the adjusted p-values.

verbose

logical; show progress.

...

further arguments passed to mirt::multipleGroup().

Value

An object of class mv_dif with elements table (one row per tested item: item, X2, df, p.value, p.adjusted, flag, esd, uesd, converged), baseline (the constrained model), models (the models with each item freed), groups, reference, focal, which.par, alpha and p_adjust. Use tidy(), gg_dif() and interpret() on it.

Details

Effect sizes are reported for two-group comparisons as the difference in expected item score between the focal and the reference group at the same ability, averaged over the focal group's ability distribution: esd is the signed difference (positive values mean the item is easier for, or favours, the focal group) and uesd the unsigned difference, which also captures crossing (non-uniform) DIF. Both are on the item score scale, so for 0/1 items they are differences in the probability of a correct answer.

Examples

# \donttest{
set.seed(1)
a <- matrix(rlnorm(8, 0.2, 0.3)); d <- matrix(rnorm(8))
d2 <- d; d2[1] <- d2[1] - 1
data <- rbind(simdata(a, d, 400, itemtype = "2PL"),
              simdata(a, d2, 400, itemtype = "2PL"))
gender <- rep(c("F", "M"), each = 400)
res <- dif(data, group = gender)
res
#> DIF analysis: F (reference) vs M; 8 items tested
#> Likelihood-ratio tests freeing a1, d; BH-adjusted p < 0.05 flags DIF
#> 
#>    item     X2 df p.value p.adjusted flag    esd  uesd converged
#>  Item_1 47.375  2  < .001     < .001  DIF -0.220 0.220      TRUE
#>  Item_2  2.735  2    .255       .529      -0.009 0.059      TRUE
#>  Item_3  1.804  2    .406       .529       0.041 0.041      TRUE
#>  Item_4  2.441  2    .295       .529       0.037 0.044      TRUE
#>  Item_5  1.885  2    .390       .529       0.039 0.040      TRUE
#>  Item_6  0.452  2    .798       .798      -0.016 0.016      TRUE
#>  Item_7  1.542  2    .463       .529      -0.023 0.043      TRUE
#>  Item_8  3.739  2    .154       .529       0.059 0.059      TRUE
gg_dif(res)

interpret(res)
#> DIF overview
#> ------------
#> * Items were tested for DIF between F and M, with F as the reference group (n
#>   = 400 F, n = 400 M). 
#> * Each item's parameters (a1, d) were freed in turn and compared with a model
#>   holding them equal across groups (likelihood-ratio test, BH-adjusted p <
#>   0.05). 
#> * On the common scale, the M group's mean ability is 0.09 SD below the F
#>   group's, and its SD is 1.23. 
#> 
#> DIF items
#> ---------
#> * 1 of 8 items show DIF: Item_1 (expected score difference -0.220, favours F;
#>   p < .001). 
#> * Statistical DIF is not proof of bias: ask content experts whether these
#>   items measure something other than the intended ability for one group
#>   before removing or revising them. 
#> 
# }
